title: Online support basics: channels, setup and safety

say: Online support basics: channels, setup and safety.
This is the video for module 1 of Online Customer Support.
Online customer support means helping customers in writing, through a screen. The customer cannot see your smile. Everything she feels comes from three things.

panel.heading: Your words are the whole experience
items: Clarity: short sentences, a clear next step

say: Speed. A quick first reply, even if it only says you are checking.

say: Clarity. Short sentences, specific facts and a clear next step.

panel.heading: Your words are the whole experience

say: Follow-through. If you say, I will update you by 2 pm, you update her by 2 pm, even if the news is still waiting. Breaking a promise does more damage than a slow first reply.

panel.heading: Your words are the whole experience
items: Clarity: short sentences, a clear next step

say: Here is a simple rule. Keep quick things quick, and move serious things to a record. A customer who asks the price of a bag on WhatsApp should get the answer on WhatsApp.
A customer who wants a refund should still get a fast, warm reply, but the refund details should be confirmed in writing where the business can find them again, by email or in your tracking sheet.
And never promise money you are not allowed to approve.
Every request, on any channel, moves through six stages. A message arrives, and you acknowledge it quickly.
You understand what she needs and check the record before you answer.
You solve it, or pass it to the right person.
You confirm with the customer, then log and close the case.

For example, Ngozi opens 7 new messages at 9 am. She scans all 7 first instead of answering the top one. Price questions get saved replies. A cracked jar gets an apology and an update promised by 2 pm. All 7 had a first reply within 30 minutes.

panel.heading: From message to closed case
panel.rule: Scan all new messages first, then prioritise.

say: Use the free WhatsApp Business app, on its own number if possible. Complete your profile and hours, and switch on a greeting and an away message.
Save quick replies for repeated questions, and always add the customer's name before sending.
Create labels: New, Waiting for customer, Waiting for us, and Resolved. Any chat still in Waiting for us at the end of the day is a promise you have not kept yet.

Scammers target both customers and businesses. First, the fake payment alert. A customer sends a screenshot and asks you to release goods quickly. Screenshots prove nothing. Confirm the money has landed in the business account.

cards.d: A screenshot and a rush to release goods. Confirm the money is in the business account first.
I sent too much, please refund the difference. Check the real balance and get owner approval.
Never share or ask for PINs, OTPs, passwords or verification codes.

say: Second, overpayment. I sent 50,000 instead of 5,000 by mistake, please refund 45,000. Check the real balance first, and refund only with the owner's approval.

cards.d: A screenshot and a rush to release goods. Confirm the money is in the business account first.
I sent too much, please refund the difference. Check the real balance and get owner approval.
Never share or ask for PINs, OTPs, passwords or verification codes.

say: Third, asking for codes. A real business never needs a customer's PIN, OTP, password or WhatsApp code. Turn on two-step verification for the business number.

cards.d: A screenshot and a rush to release goods. Confirm the money is in the business account first.
I sent too much, please refund the difference. Check the real balance and get owner approval.
Never share or ask for PINs, OTPs, passwords or verification codes.

say: Bisi gets an order and an urgent request. The customer says he is travelling in one hour.
The order is 4 power banks at 18,000 naira each, which is 72,000. He sends a screenshot of a 72,000 transfer. Bisi replies: we will dispatch as soon as the payment reflects in our business account.
The owner checks the bank app. After 20 minutes, nothing has arrived. The customer becomes aggressive, then stops replying.
No goods were lost. The urgency and the pressure were warning signs. The business account was the only proof that counted.
To remember. Keep your three promises. Scan first, then prioritise problems and money matters. Personalise every quick reply. Confirm payment only in the business account.
And collect only the personal data you need, and never post a customer's chat or receipt anywhere.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Payment confirmed in the business account only
Collect only the data you need; keep it secure

say: Your turn. Map the channels your business uses. Set up the profile, greeting and away messages. Save at least 5 quick replies and create the four labels.
Then write a payment reply that says you never ask for PINs or codes, and a calm boundary message for abusive chats.
Continue with the lessons below.
